question: True or false: on the border between France and Spain there's a small island that switches countries every six months.
source_excerpt: Its sovereignty alternates between the two countries every six months.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume borders are fixed lines and that a place belongs to one country. Here an island takes turns between two countries on a schedule, which sounds made up but is true.
extra.verification_notes: Pheasant Island in the Bidasoa is a Franco-Spanish condominium whose sovereignty alternates every six months, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheasant_Island.

explanation: Pheasant Island in the Bidasoa river is ruled by Spain for half the year and by France for the other half. The arrangement comes from a 17th-century peace treaty signed on the island itself.

question: You drive west from Spain across the border into Portugal. What should you do to your watch?
source_excerpt: Spain is one hour ahead of Portugal, and the gap should hold through 2026 because both countries shift clocks on the same dates.

extra.why_interesting: The two countries sit side by side on the same longitudes, so players expect no time change at all. The real answer is a one-hour jump, explained by a political decision rather than geography.
extra.verification_notes: Mainland Spain (CET) is one hour ahead of mainland Portugal (WET), so going west you set your watch back one hour; both countries change clocks on the same dates in 2026 (https://www.thelocal.es/20260326/when-do-the-clocks-change-next-in-spain-in-2026).

explanation: Spain runs on the same clock as Berlin and Paris even though it lies as far west as Portugal and Britain. Spain switched to that time zone in 1940 and never switched back.

question: Only one US state shares a land border with exactly one other state. Which state is it?
source_excerpt: Maine is bordered by New Hampshire to the western southwest, the Gulf of Maine to the southeast, and the Canadian provinces of New Brunswick and Quebec

extra.why_interesting: It sounds like trivia, but a player can work it out by picturing the US map: the state has to sit in a corner, tucked behind Canada and the ocean, and the north-east tip fits.
extra.verification_notes: Maine's only state neighbor is New Hampshire; no other state has exactly one bordering state (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine).

explanation: Maine, in the far north-east corner, is boxed in by Canada and the Atlantic, so New Hampshire is its only US neighbour. Alaska and Hawaii don't count, because they border no states at all.

question: France's longest land border isn't with any European country at all. Which country is it shared with?
source_excerpt: Not verified by live search; figures recalled from memory (CIA World Factbook: Brazil 649 km, Spain 623 km).

extra.why_interesting: Players picture mainland France and guess Spain, Belgium or Germany. The stem says the answer is outside Europe, which lets them reason their way to French Guiana and then to its bigger neighbour. The answer lands as an 'I can work this out' moment.
extra.verification_notes: France's longest land border is with Brazil (French Guiana, ~650-730 km), longer than Spain (~623 km); source figures vary but the ranking doesn't change. Not checked with live search.

explanation: French Guiana in South America is a full part of France, and its border with Brazil runs about 730 kilometres, longer than France's border with Spain. So in a sense, Brazil is France's biggest neighbour.
